## LogDigest Workflow Summary

**What it does:** Automatically transforms massive build/test/deploy log files into actionable root-cause analysis with owner assignment and next-step commands.

**Pattern demonstrated:** Sequential pipeline pattern - a collector agent gathers and filters log data, then a summarizer agent performs intelligent analysis to produce structured insights.

**Real-world use case:** When CI/CD pipelines fail, developers waste time digging through thousands of log lines hunting for the actual problem. This workflow instantly digests those logs into ranked hypotheses about what went wrong, identifies the likely owning team, and suggests specific commands to run for investigation or fixes.

**Why reach for this instead of a script:** Traditional scripts rely on brittle regex patterns that break when new tools or error formats appear. This uses AI agents that understand context and can correlate errors across different log sections, providing human-readable analysis with confidence levels. It adapts to new error patterns without code changes and handles the nuanced reasoning required to distinguish root causes from symptoms.

The workflow elegantly combines shell automation (log collection) with AI reasoning (analysis), making it perfect for DevOps teams who need fast incident triage without manual log archaeology.

  "pattern": "Sequential pipeline pattern with collector and analyzer agents",
  "useCase": "DevOps incident triage - instantly digest failed CI/CD logs into ranked hypotheses, team assignments, and concrete debugging commands instead of manual log archaeology"
}

## Standards Reviewer Workflow

**What it does:** Automatically reviews PR diffs against repository-specific standards files (CLAUDE.md, style guides, architecture docs) and reports only violations with explanations.

**Pattern:** Sequential pipeline pattern with two stages: standards discovery/loading followed by intelligent diff review against those standards.

**Real-world use case:** Enforcing code quality and architectural consistency without manual oversight. Instead of hoping developers remember all the repo's style guides and architectural constraints, this workflow automatically finds standards files, extracts rules, and checks every changed line against them. It catches violations that static analysis tools miss because it understands context and intent.

**Why use this instead of a script:** Traditional linters only catch syntax issues, but this workflow uses AI agents to understand nuanced standards written in natural language. It can parse CLAUDE.md files, architectural decision records, and style guides in any format, then intelligently apply those rules to code changes. The structured output includes severity levels and clear explanations, making it actionable for developers.

This is particularly powerful for teams that have evolved complex, domain-specific standards that can't be encoded in ESLint rules or similar tools.

**Pattern**: Sequential pipeline - a classic two-step dependency chain where the writing task consumes the structured output from the research task.

## Alert Suppressor Workflow Summary

**What it does:** Intelligently filters incoming monitoring alerts by deduplicating, cross-referencing against incident history and noise patterns, then routing only novel or high-risk alerts to on-call engineers.

**Pattern:** This demonstrates a **pipeline with parallel preprocessing** pattern. It runs deduplication and context lookup in parallel, then sequences through classification and dispatch stages, ending with a summary report.

**Real-world use case:** Solves alert fatigue for DevOps/SRE teams by preventing duplicate alerts and known noise from waking up engineers at 3am. Instead of every alert triggering a page, it uses AI agents to intelligently classify alerts against incident history, only escalating genuinely concerning issues while filing tickets for lower-priority items.

**Why reach for this instead of a script:** The multi-agent architecture handles complex decision-making that would be brittle in a traditional script. Each agent specializes in different tasks (context lookup, classification, dispatch) with access to different tools. The structured data validation, parallel processing, and AI-powered classification would require significant infrastructure in a custom script, while Smithers provides it out of the box with clear separation of concerns and built-in observability.

## PR Shepherd Workflow Summary

This workflow automates comprehensive PR review by gathering context in parallel and producing structured feedback.

**What it does:** Automatically reviews pull requests by collecting diff information, test results, and PR metadata in parallel, then generates structured review comments categorized by severity and type, and determines approval status.

**Pattern:** Fan-out-fan-in - The workflow fans out to gather three types of context simultaneously (diff analysis, test results, PR metadata), then fans back in to perform structured review analysis and generate a final report.

**Real-world use case:** Provides consistent, thorough automated code reviews that catch bugs, security issues, and performance problems before human reviewers see the PR. Perfect for teams wanting to standardize review quality and catch issues early in large codebases.

**Why choose this over a script:** Scripts would run sequentially (much slower), lack structured error handling, and require significant boilerplate for parallel execution and failure recovery. This workflow's parallel context gathering, built-in retry logic, and maintainable MDX prompts make it far more robust and efficient than custom automation.

  "useCase": "Provides consistent, thorough automated code reviews that catch bugs, security issues, and performance problems before human reviewers see the PR, perfect for teams wanting to standardize review quality and catch issues early in large codebases."
}
```

## Error Clusterer Workflow Summary

**What it does:** Automatically ingests error logs from CI/API/runtime sources, groups similar errors into clusters, analyzes root causes, and builds a searchable knowledge base with remediation steps.

**Pattern:** **Pipeline pattern** — A linear 4-stage data processing pipeline: ingest → cluster → explain → update. Each stage transforms the data further, from raw logs to structured knowledge.

**Real-world use case:** Solves error triage chaos during production incidents. Instead of SRE teams manually sifting through hundreds of duplicate errors, this workflow automatically deduplicates them, identifies patterns, and builds institutional knowledge that prevents future fire-drills.

**Why reach for this vs. a script:** Goes way beyond simple log aggregation. It provides intelligent error fingerprinting that strips variable parts (timestamps, request IDs) to find true duplicates, uses AI agents to analyze root causes and suggest specific remediation steps, automatically maintains a searchable KB, and creates tickets. The orchestration of multiple processing phases with type-safe schemas would be painful to build from scratch.

This is the difference between "here are your logs" and "here's what's broken and how to fix it."

```json
{
  "name": "error-clusterer",
  "source": "examples",
  "filePath": "examples/error-clusterer.jsx",
  "summary": "Automatically ingests error logs from CI/API/runtime sources, groups similar errors into clusters, analyzes root causes, and builds a searchable knowledge base with remediation steps.",
  "pattern": "pipeline",

## Retry Budget Manager Workflow Summary

**What it does**: Intelligently manages retry attempts for failing operations with smart budget tracking, failure classification, and escalation when retries become wasteful.

**Pattern**: Adaptive retry loop with policy control — the workflow loops through step execution and policy evaluation, with escalation breaking out when needed.

**Real-world use case**: Handles retry logic for unreliable operations like API calls, payment processing, or distributed job queues where you need more than just exponential backoff.

**Why reach for this instead of a script**: A script gives you dumb exponential backoff or fixed retry counts. This workflow provides intelligent failure classification (transient vs persistent vs quota), adaptive retry policies based on failure type, budget management to prevent infinite waste, and proper escalation with detailed analysis and recommendations.

The workflow uses three specialized agents:
- **Step Runner**: Executes operations and classifies failures accurately 
- **Policy Controller**: Makes intelligent retry decisions based on failure class and remaining budget
- **Escalation Agent**: Provides actionable analysis when retries should stop

This turns retry logic from a simple loop into a smart system that learns from failures and makes good decisions about when to keep trying vs when to escalate.

  "pattern": "adaptive retry loop with policy control",
  "useCase": "Handles retry logic for unreliable operations like API calls, payment processing, or distributed job queues where you need more than just exponential backoff."
}

Based on reading the `fail-only-report.jsx` workflow, here's a concise summary:

## Summary

**What it does**: Runs commands in parallel (tests, linting, etc.) and only invokes expensive failure analysis agents when something actually fails — keeping green runs cheap and quiet.

**Pattern**: Conditional pipeline with smart branching — the workflow runs all commands, analyzes results for notable events (failures/regressions), then branches to either generate a detailed root-cause report or skip the expensive analysis entirely.

**Real-world use case**: Cost-efficient CI/CD monitoring where you want to minimize compute costs on successful builds while still getting detailed failure analysis when things break. Perfect for teams running hundreds of builds daily who don't want to pay for analysis on every green build.

**Why reach for this instead of a script**: A script would either always run the expensive analysis (wasteful) or never run it (unhelpful when failures occur). This workflow gives you the best of both worlds — intelligent conditional behavior with proper orchestration, state management, and the ability to route results to different sinks (PR comments, Slack, issues) based on the outcome.

The workflow demonstrates how Smithers can optimize operational costs by making infrastructure decisions based on actual results rather than running everything blindly.

```json
{
  "name": "fail-only-report",
  "source": "examples",
  "filePath": "fail-only-report.jsx",
  "summary": "Runs commands in parallel and only generates expensive failure analysis reports when something actually fails or regresses, keeping green runs cheap and quiet",
  "pattern": "conditional pipeline with smart branching",
  "useCase": "Cost-efficient CI/CD monitoring that minimizes compute costs on successful builds while providing detailed root-cause analysis for failures"
}
```

## Summary

This workflow scans all Smithers workflow examples, ranks them by utility and wow factor, drafts a countdown tweet thread about the top ones, and optionally posts it to Twitter/X with timed delays between tweets.

**Pattern**: Fan-out-fan-in with timing controls. It fans out to summarize workflows in parallel (max 10 concurrency), fans in to rank and draft the thread, then posts tweets with 30-second delays between each.

**Real-world use case**: Automated social media content creation for developer advocates or engineering teams who want to showcase their work in structured countdown format. Perfect for release announcements, "best-of" showcases, or regular content marketing.

**Why reach for this instead of a script**: The built-in orchestration handles concurrency limits, caching (prevents re-work when files unchanged), error handling with `continueOnFail`, timer-based posting with proper threading, structured outputs with Zod validation, and multi-phase pipeline dependencies. A script would need hundreds of lines to handle all these orchestration concerns properly.

```json

  "pattern": "Fan-out-fan-in with timing controls",
  "useCase": "Automated social media content creation for developer advocates or engineering teams who want to showcase their work in structured countdown format, perfect for release announcements or regular content marketing."
}
```

This Smithers workflow automates prompt engineering through systematic iteration and evaluation.

## Summary

**What it does**: Automatically generates prompt variants, tests them against a dataset, and iteratively refines them until hitting a target performance score.

**Pattern**: **Iterative optimization loop** — a generate → evaluate → optimize cycle that continues until success criteria are met or max iterations reached.

**Real-world use case**: Eliminates the guesswork from prompt engineering. Instead of manually tweaking prompts and hoping for better results, this systematically finds the optimal prompt by running structured evaluations against test cases. Perfect for teams that need reliable, high-performing prompts for production systems.

**Why not just a script**: Scripts are brittle one-offs. This workflow provides structured evaluation with scoring, multi-agent orchestration (separate generator, evaluator, and optimizer agents), built-in iteration control, and comprehensive reporting. It turns prompt optimization from an art into a repeatable engineering process with measurable outcomes.

The workflow uses three specialized agents working in concert: a prompt generator creates candidates, an evaluator scores them against test cases, and an optimizer analyzes failures to make targeted improvements. This creates a robust feedback loop that converges on high-quality prompts.

```json
{
  "name": "prompt-optimizer-harness",
  "source": "examples",
  "filePath": "examples/prompt-optimizer-harness.jsx",
  "summary": "Automatically generates prompt variants, tests them against a dataset, and iteratively refines them until hitting a target performance score.",
  "pattern": "Iterative optimization loop",
  "useCase": "Eliminates guesswork from prompt engineering by systematically finding optimal prompts through structured evaluation against test cases."
}
```

## Support Deflector Workflow Summary

**What it does:** Automatically triages support tickets by classifying them, retrieving relevant knowledge base articles, drafting responses, and only escalating to humans when risk or uncertainty is high.

**Pattern:** This demonstrates a **pipeline with conditional branching** pattern. The workflow runs a sequential pipeline (classify → retrieve knowledge → draft response) then uses a complex branching decision based on multiple risk factors (confidence levels, sentiment, coverage scores) to determine whether to auto-reply or escalate to human agents.

**Real-world use case:** This solves the support team overwhelm problem where 70-80% of tickets could be handled automatically if you had smart enough triage. It's perfect for SaaS companies drowning in "how do I reset my password" tickets while ensuring genuinely complex issues still get human attention.

**Why reach for this over a script:** A script would be a nightmare to maintain for this complexity. You'd need to orchestrate multiple AI agents with different specializations, handle structured outputs with proper validation, implement sophisticated multi-factor escalation logic, and manage the conditional branching. The declarative Smithers approach makes this readable and maintainable, while a script would become an unmaintainable mess of nested conditionals and API calls.

The workflow showcases how AI orchestration can handle nuanced business logic that would be brittle in traditional automation - like detecting when a customer is truly angry vs just direct, or when knowledge coverage is insufficient for a confident response.

```json
{
  "name": "Support Deflector",
  "source": "examples",
  "filePath": "examples/support-deflector.jsx",
  "summary": "Automatically triages support tickets by classifying them, retrieving relevant knowledge base articles, drafting responses, and only escalating to humans when risk or uncertainty is high.",
  "pattern": "pipeline with conditional branching",
  "useCase": "Solves support team overwhelm by intelligently handling routine tickets while ensuring complex/risky issues get human attention. Perfect for SaaS companies drowning in repetitive support requests."
}
```

## Lead Router with Approval Workflow

**What it does:** This workflow automatically scores and routes inbound sales leads while requiring human approval for borderline cases.

**Pattern:** Review loop / approval gate - a linear pipeline that conditionally branches to human intervention based on AI scoring.

**Real-world use case:** Solves the lead qualification bottleneck that every growing company faces. Instead of manually reviewing every inbound lead (doesn't scale) or fully automating everything (misses nuanced decisions), it handles clear winners/losers automatically but flags uncertain cases for human judgment.

**Why not just write a script:** A script would break on messy, real-world lead data - varying form formats, incomplete fields, ambiguous company information. This uses AI agents that can parse unstructured input, make nuanced scoring decisions, and handle the approval workflow with proper UI integration. The declarative structure makes business logic transparent and easily adjustable.

The workflow demonstrates how to build scalable automation that keeps humans in the loop where their judgment matters most, while eliminating grunt work on obvious decisions.

```json
{
  "name": "lead-router-with-approval",
  "source": "examples",
  "filePath": "examples/lead-router-with-approval.jsx",
  "summary": "Automatically scores and routes inbound sales leads while requiring human approval for borderline cases",
  "pattern": "review loop / approval gate",
  "useCase": "Lead qualification bottleneck - scales lead processing while keeping humans in the loop for edge cases that need nuanced judgment"
}
```

Based on my analysis of the `receipt-stream-watcher.jsx` workflow, here's a concise summary:

## Summary

**What it does**: This workflow extracts structured data from receipt images/text using streaming processing and routes receipts to downstream systems as soon as enough high-confidence fields are captured.

**Pattern**: Streaming extraction with early exit - it demonstrates a partial-state consumer pattern where the workflow doesn't wait for complete data extraction but makes routing decisions based on confidence thresholds and field availability.

**Real-world use case**: Enterprise expense management where receipts need fast routing to expense reports, reimbursement flows, or audit queues. Instead of waiting for full OCR completion, it can route receipts for processing as soon as core fields (merchant, total, date, currency) are identified with 85%+ confidence.

**Why choose this over a script**: A traditional script processes receipts linearly and waits for complete extraction. This workflow handles streaming data, coordinates multiple specialized agents (extractor → consumer → router), and implements sophisticated confidence-based routing logic that would be complex to maintain in a monolithic script. It also provides structured schemas and can gracefully handle partial failures while still making progress on high-confidence data.

The workflow excels at real-time document processing where speed matters more than completeness - perfect for high-volume receipt processing where waiting for perfect extraction would create bottlenecks.

  "pattern": "Streaming extraction with early exit and partial-state consumer",
  "useCase": "Enterprise expense management for fast routing of receipts to expense reports, reimbursement flows, or audit queues based on confidence thresholds rather than waiting for complete OCR processing."
}
```

Looking at this workflow, I can see it's a sophisticated documentation maintenance system that automatically keeps docs synchronized with code changes.

## Analysis

**What it does:** Detects API/CLI changes in code and automatically patches affected documentation to keep it current, then creates a review PR.

**Pattern demonstrated:** Sequential pipeline with parallel fan-out. It runs detect → patch in sequence, then fans out to verification and PR creation in parallel.

**Real-world use case:** When you ship API changes, CLI updates, or SDK modifications, documentation becomes stale instantly. This workflow catches those changes and intelligently rewrites the affected docs, preserving prose and formatting while updating code examples and references.

**Why reach for this over a script:** AI agents can understand semantic context and make nuanced text updates that would break a regex-based script. It handles complex scenarios like preserving surrounding prose, understanding when config shapes change, and creating meaningful PR descriptions with checklists. A traditional script couldn't handle the contextual understanding needed to rewrite documentation properly.

The workflow is particularly clever in its parallel final stage - while one agent verifies the patches for correctness, another creates the PR, maximizing efficiency. The structured schemas ensure reliable data flow between stages.

```json
{
  "name": "DocsPatcher",
  "source": "examples",
  "filePath": "examples/docs-patcher.jsx",
  "summary": "Detects API/CLI changes in code and automatically patches affected documentation to keep it current, then creates a review PR.",
  "pattern": "Sequential pipeline with parallel fan-out",
  "useCase": "Automated documentation maintenance - keeping docs synchronized with API changes, CLI updates, and SDK modifications without manual intervention."
}
```

## Compliance Evidence Collector Summary

**What it does:** Automates regulatory compliance evidence collection by orchestrating parallel data gathering from APIs, MCP tools, and browser fallbacks, then assembling findings into structured audit packets.

**Pattern:** Fan-out-fan-in orchestration - a planning phase fans out to parallel evidence collection across multiple sources, then fans back in through normalization into a final compliance packet.

**Real-world use case:** SOC 2 audits, ISO 27001 reviews, PCI-DSS assessments - any regulatory compliance process that requires gathering evidence from multiple systems (cloud providers, SaaS tools, internal APIs) and consolidating it into audit-ready documentation.

**Why this beats a script:** Handles the coordination nightmare of collecting from dozens of different sources with varying APIs, built-in fallback strategies when APIs fail, structured schemas that ensure audit-quality output, and parallel execution with proper error handling and timeouts. A script would be brittle and require manual coordination of all the async collection and normalization steps.

This workflow turns compliance evidence gathering from a weeks-long manual slog into an automated pipeline that produces audit-ready packets in hours.

## Summary

**What it does:** Creates a "boss" agent that breaks down complex software development goals into tasks, assigns them to specialized worker agents (coder, tester, docs writer), and supervises their parallel execution with retry logic.

**Pattern:** Supervisor/worker pattern with dynamic delegation and review cycles. The boss agent plans → delegates to parallel workers in isolated worktrees → reviews results → re-delegates failures in a loop.

**Real-world use case:** Manages complex software development projects that require multiple specialized skills - coding, testing, and documentation. Instead of you manually coordinating different types of work, the supervisor orchestrates everything while maintaining oversight and adapting to failures.

**Why reach for this instead of a script:** A script would handle tasks sequentially and couldn't make intelligent decisions about task decomposition, failure recovery, or dynamic re-delegation based on results. This provides intelligent project management that can adapt strategies, retry failures, and coordinate multiple specialized agents working in parallel - like having an AI technical lead manage your development team.
